findings.summary: The left (base tables) lower-X window is centred on EFIT's null, and this arm's solved lower null lies 2.1 cm above the window's top edge (solved Z = -1.11615 m against a window top of -1.13769 m), so the panel carries the solved field only as two clipped blue stubs at the top edge and draws no solved-null marker; a reader comparing the two zoom panels sees one null set in the left one. The full-field panel beside it does draw the solved null marker, and the 8.115 cm offset the row reports is the reason the null left the window, so the figure as a whole still carries both null sets.

The legend explains the filled solved null, the hollow EFIT square and the hollow-circle shadow nodes, but the full-field panels also draw each arm's other qualified nulls hollow in the same X and square vocabulary; a hollow blue X at the vessel top therefore has no legend entry and can be read as a solved-null marker that failed to fill rather than as the second saddle.

The panel notes label the left arm 'base tables' while the evidence caption calls the same arm 'capped'; a reader moving between the figure and its caption has to infer that the two names denote one arm, and the section text uses 'capped' throughout.

At the top-left of the left (base tables) full-field panel, the upper-saddle marker, the solved axis triangle and two hollow shadow-node circles bunch within a few pixels of one another and over the wall, so no single mark there is separable at a glance. The cluster sits well away from the lower-X subject that the figure is about.
